title: UBS sees S&P 500 at 8,400 by June as AI and earnings extend record rally
key_facts: UBS expects the S&P 500 to reach 8,400 by June next year, according to a note published before Wednesday's US session (7 Oct 2026).
The S&P 500 gained 0.6% on Tuesday to its first record high since August, taking its gain this year to about 14%.
UBS forecasts global AI-related capital spending to rise by more than a third to $1.2 trillion in 2027.
UBS estimates S&P 500 earnings will rise 25% this year and 14% in 2027; it forecasts US growth of 2.2% this year and 2% in 2027.
UBS favours consumer discretionary, financials and industrials, plus health care and utilities as defensive holdings.

Since the note, Fed minutes showed most officials see another hike as likely by year-end, US consumer inflation expectations rose, and Axios reported the Pentagon has readied options to resume strikes on Iran.
quote_evidence: UBS expects the US equity rally to continue despite rising interest rates and conflict in the Middle East, forecasting the S&P 500 will reach 8,400 by June next year, according to a note published before Wednesday's US session.
Whether earnings growth can keep outrunning higher rates and oil risk will decide if UBS's target is met.
why_it_matters_hint: A bank's bullish index target rests on earnings outrunning higher rates and oil risk; the Fed minutes point the other way.
notes: Read in full on investingLive. The forecast is UBS's own note; the Fed minutes and the Axios report are cited by the article, not checked here.
